stem: In human-centered design frameworks, what is the primary distinction between usability and user experience (UX)?

options.text: Usability is the broader discipline that contains UX, which is limited to a product's visual design.
options.rationale: The relationship is reversed: UX is the broader discipline, and usability is one part of it focused on ease of use.

options.text: Usability covers a product's technical reliability and speed, while UX covers the ease of completing tasks with it.
options.rationale: Ease of completing tasks is the core of usability, while technical reliability and speed are engineering qualities rather than the scope of UX.

options.text: Usability covers task efficiency, learnability, and error reduction; UX covers the whole emotional journey of a product.
options.shortLabel: Task efficiency vs complete holistic journey
options.rationale: Usability is a key sub-discipline within user experience that ensures a tool works smoothly, while UX covers the entire emotional and practical lifecycle of interaction.

options.text: Usability and UX are interchangeable terms for how easily people can use a product.
options.rationale: The terms were once used interchangeably, but usability is now understood as a sub-discipline contributing to UX, not a synonym for it.

explanation: Usability is a sub-discipline of user experience focused on whether a user can learn, navigate, and complete tasks easily, quickly, and without error. User experience (UX) is a broader, holistic discipline that encompasses usability, accessibility, content utility, emotional response, brand trust, and overall satisfaction.

references.title: Usability: A Part of the User Experience
